module1.title: Linux Navigation
module1.story: Orientation day. IT dropped you into a workstation with a maze of folders and no map. Before they'll grant you real access, you need to prove you can find your own way around.
module1.mission: Locate the onboarding key hidden somewhere inside your home directory.

objectives.label: Print your current directory with pwd
Read the hidden key file with cat

hints: pwd tells you where you are right now — start there.
ls -la will reveal hidden files too, not just the obvious ones.
The key lives at records/logs/archive/.keyfile — cd there and cat it.

module2.title: File Operations
module2.story: The workstation from Module 1 is now yours, but it's a mess. Your supervisor wants the inbox cleaned up: organize what matters, discard what doesn't.
module2.mission: Create a backup folder, copy the manifest into it, move the draft into its final form, and delete the junk file.
hints: mkdir -p can create the whole workspace/backup path in one shot.
cp inbox/manifest.txt workspace/backup/ keeps the original in place.
mv both renames and relocates — use it to turn draft.txt into workspace/final.txt.
The key is hidden in a dotfile: ls -a in module2/.vault

module3.title: Searching & Filtering
module3.story: Someone on the team logged an access key deep inside a pile of rotated log files and now nobody remembers which one. Your job: find it without opening every file by hand.
module3.mission: Use find, grep, and head/tail to locate the log line containing the access key.

objectives.label: Use find to search the data directory
Use grep to filter file contents
Use head or tail to inspect a file

hints: find /home/student/module3/data -type f lists every log file, however deep.
grep -r 'ACCESS_KEY' /home/student/module3/data searches recursively in one command.
Once you've narrowed it down, tail the specific file to read the last lines.

module4.title: Permissions & Shell Scripting
module4.story: A deployment script has been sitting broken for weeks because nobody fixed its permissions or ran it as the right user. Fix it and let it do its job.
module4.mission: Make run.sh executable, fix report.txt's ownership, and run the script to unlock the key.

objectives.label: Change the owner of data/report.txt with chown
Execute run.sh so it unlocks the key

hints: chmod +x scripts/run.sh grants execute permission.
sudo chown student data/report.txt changes the owner (you'll need sudo).
Run the script with ./run.sh once it's executable — check what file it creates.

module5.title: Advanced Linux
module5.story: Capstone day. A misbehaving background process is eating resources, and the only way to identify and stop it — then extract what it left behind — is by combining everything you've learned so far.
module5.mission: Find the runaway process, kill it, then pipe and redirect your way to the final key.

objectives.label: Use ps or top to inspect running processes
Use kill to stop the runaway process
Chain commands together with a pipe (|)
Use awk or sed with output redirection

hints: ps aux will show you the runaway sleep process and its PID.
kill <pid> stops it — the PID is also saved in module5/.runaway_pid.
Try: cat .final/key.txt | awk '{print $1}' — combine pipes and redirection to explore.

python_module1.title: Python Basics: print, variables, input
python_module1.story: Welcome to the Python track. Let's start with basic input, variables, and printing output.
python_module1.mission: Create a Python script named module1/python/main.py that takes input and prints it.

objectives.label: Run main.py using python3 at least once
The program reads standard input and prints it back

hints: Use the standard input() function to read from stdin, store it in a variable, and use print() to print it.
Make sure your file path is exactly /home/student/module1/python/main.py.

python_module2.title: Python Control Flow: conditions & loops
python_module2.story: Time to add logic to your scripts. Using if-else conditions and loops allows you to repeat and fork code blocks.
python_module2.mission: Create /home/student/module2/python/loops.py to loop numbers 1 to 10 and print whether they are even or odd.

objectives.label: Print whether numbers are even or odd

hints: Use a for i in range(1, 11): loop to iterate through the numbers.
Use the modulo operator % to determine if a number is even or odd (e.g. i % 2 == 0).

python_module3.title: Python Collections: functions, lists, dicts
python_module3.story: Functions organize your code, while lists and dictionaries let you store complex data structures.
python_module3.mission: Create /home/student/module3/python/collections.py defining lists, dicts, and a custom function.

objectives.label: Define at least one list and one dictionary
Define a custom function using def keyword

hints: A list is declared with square brackets: my_list = [...].
A dictionary uses curly braces: my_dict = {...}.
Define functions using the def keyword, e.g. def my_func():.

python_module4.title: Python Robustness: files, imports, exceptions
python_module4.story: Production scripts need to read files from disk and handle errors gracefully.
python_module4.mission: Create /home/student/module4/python/files.py to read /home/student/module4/python/data.txt inside a try-except block.

objectives.label: Wrap code in a try-except block

hints: Use with open('/home/student/module4/python/data.txt', 'r') as f: inside your try block.
Catch FileNotFoundError in your except block and print a user-friendly error message.

python_module5.title: Python OS & Automation Challenge
python_module5.story: Python is widely used for system administration. The os and subprocess modules let you automate shell operations.
python_module5.mission: Create /home/student/module5/python/script.py using os/subprocess to execute system operations.

objectives.label: Call os.system or subprocess function to run shell commands

hints: Use import subprocess at the top.
Call subprocess.run(['ls', '-la']) or os.system('ls -la') to run a basic command.

c_module1.title: C Basics: printf, scanf, variables
c_module1.story: Welcome to the C track. C is compiled and fast, but requires type declarations and memory consideration.
c_module1.mission: Create /home/student/module1/c/main.c, compile to app, and test user input using scanf.

objectives.label: Compile main.c using gcc into app
Program reads standard input and prints it with printf

hints: Write a standard C main function and include <stdio.h>.
Compile your code using: gcc main.c -o app

c_module2.title: C Control Flow: Conditions & Loops
c_module2.story: Implement decision making in C using if-else conditions and iterate using loops.
c_module2.mission: Create /home/student/module2/c/loops.c containing a loop that compiles and executes successfully.

objectives.label: Execute app and verify loop output

hints: Write a basic for loop in C: for(int i = 0; i < 10; i++) { ... }.
Compile with gcc loops.c -o app and run with ./app.

c_module3.title: C Structures: Functions & Arrays
c_module3.story: Functions break down complexity in C, while arrays store collections of similar data types.
c_module3.mission: Create /home/student/module3/c/arrays.c defining a custom function and an array.

objectives.label: Define an array in the source file

hints: An array is declared like: int numbers[5] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};.
Declare your custom function before main() or write a function prototype.

c_module4.title: C Memory: Pointers & Allocation
c_module4.story: Pointers hold memory addresses and are key to data structures in C.
c_module4.mission: Create /home/student/module4/c/pointers.c to practice pointer syntax and dereferencing.

objectives.label: De-reference a pointer (* ptr) or call malloc

hints: Use the dereference operator * to modify the value pointed to by a pointer.
Example pointer usage: int val = 10; int *ptr = &val; *ptr = 20;

c_module5.title: C Programming Challenge
c_module5.story: Showcase your C proficiency by completing a final coding challenge.
c_module5.mission: Create /home/student/module5/c/challenge.c, compile and execute it successfully.
hints: Ensure you have a main function that returns 0 upon success.
Verify compiling with: gcc challenge.c -o app.

cpp_module1.title: C++ Basics: cout & cin
cpp_module1.story: Welcome to the C++ track. C++ introduces streams and object-oriented features on top of C.
cpp_module1.mission: Create /home/student/module1/cpp/main.cpp, compile it, and process input using cin and cout.

objectives.label: Compile main.cpp using g++ into app
Use cout and cin to print input

hints: Include <iostream> and use std::cout and std::cin.
Compile using g++: g++ main.cpp -o app

cpp_module2.title: C++ Control Flow: loops & functions
cpp_module2.story: C++ supports loops and robust procedural programming features through functions.

objectives.label: Define a custom function in the source file

hints: Define a helper function like void showMessage() { ... } and call it from main.

cpp_module3.title: C++ OOP: Classes & Objects
cpp_module3.story: Classes are the building blocks of C++ OOP, encapsulating data and functions.
cpp_module3.mission: Create /home/student/module3/cpp/classes.cpp defining a simple C++ class.

objectives.label: Define a class in the source file

hints: Declare a class Student or similar: class Student { public: ... private: ... };.

cpp_module4.title: C++ STL: Vectors & Streams
cpp_module4.story: The Standard Template Library (STL) provides powerful containers like vectors and file stream utilities.
hints: Add #include <vector> to use dynamic arrays: std::vector<int> vec;.

cpp_module5.title: C++ Capstone Challenge
cpp_module5.story: Showcase your C++ proficiency by completing a final programming challenge.
cpp_module5.mission: Create /home/student/module5/cpp/challenge.cpp, compile and execute it successfully.
hints: Verify compiling with: g++ challenge.cpp -o app.
